title: SEA-TS: Self-Evolving Agent for Autonomous Code Generation of Time Series Forecasting Algorithms

mechanism.domainTask: Autonomous code generation and optimization for time-series forecasting models
mechanism.populationDetail: An explicit MCTS tree maintains candidate-program parent-child structure; the paper also adds an Island Model with periodic migration, but does not fully specify the tree/island organization.
mechanism.archiveDetail: A MAP-Elites archive indexes candidates by architecture type, feature-engineering sophistication, and training sophistication, retaining the best solution per cell.
mechanism.replacementDetail: New candidates are inserted as MCTS tree nodes; the separate QD archive replaces each cell's incumbent only with a better solution. Island migration is reported but underspecified.
mechanism.generationDetail: One UCT-selected parent program is the branch being expanded; the LLM is prompted to return a complete forecasting implementation, while sibling, global-best/worst, and archive candidates are contextual references.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: The task metric is normalized into a historical Metric Advantage; runtime/review bug flags replace reward with -1. Review findings and global comparisons are consolidated into a running prompt used by subsequent generations.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: UCT traverses the search tree from its root to select one leaf for expansion; additional global and archive candidates condition generation but are not true parents.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/SEA-TS Self-Evolving Agent for Autonomous Code Generation of Time Series Forecasting Algorithms.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The survey currently lists SEA-TS under static role-based multi-model assignment. The paper specifies GPT-5 for generation/review and calls Qwen3-coder-plus an alternative, but does not establish fixed distinct model-to-role assignments, collaboration, or routing policy. The stated Island Model is not detailed enough to reconstruct its topology relative to the MCTS tree; the survey's tree-plus-flat-pool wording should also be checked because the paper does not clearly describe a separate flat pool.
